source.title: Weight-norm Criticality: A Mechanism for Loss Spikes Induced by the Normalization and Weight Decay
source.authors: Xiaolong Li; Zhang-Chen Zhou; Zhi-qin John Xu

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the Edge of Stability criterion as part of its analysis, but its experiments vary weight decay and normalization rather than testing the claim versions’ stated effects of width, depth, initialization, learning rate, or batch normalization on training error or speed.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss spikes and related optimization measurements under weight-decay and normalization conditions. These findings concern training instability, but do not test any listed version as stated. The paper also cites prior results; those are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Edge of Stability criterion to develop a weight-norm mechanism for loss spikes. Its own experiments measure weight-decay effects, curvature scaling and spike-boundary alignment; they do not establish V5's above-initial-threshold recovery, sustained threshold hovering while loss falls, or divergence despite starting below threshold. Normalization comparisons do not measure V6's accuracy gains or learning-rate tolerance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors propose that decay shrinks scale-invariant parameter norms, amplifies curvature and can produce spikes after critical boundary crossings. Direct temporal boundary comparisons are presented for MNIST and synthetic FNNs; Transformer and ResNet experiments provide complementary spike, scaling and intervention evidence rather than equally direct validation of every boundary.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates weight-decay-induced loss spikes and curvature in normalized networks, rather than the listed versions’ tests of training error, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate recovery, or batch-normalization speed.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with weight-decay strength, presence and type of normalization, which parameters receive weight decay, and scale-invariant layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing weight decay produces more frequent or pronounced loss spikes in normalized networks; the non-normalized MNIST control does not reliably show this behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization and weight decay can interact to induce training-loss spikes.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger decay increases endpoint curvature in the main settings; shrinking scale-invariant parameters increases curvature, and their Hessian block becomes dominant during synthetic training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shrinking scale-invariant parameters can amplify curvature in networks containing normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Sustained crossings of layer-specific spike boundaries align with loss disturbances, with interval filtering used in the MNIST analysis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-specific weight norms and gradient-direction curvature can indicate weight-decay-induced loss spikes.

fits_no_version.finding: Excluding MLP or scale-invariant parameters from decay reduces spikes; restricting decay to the output layer removes a clear increasing endpoint-sharpness trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of weight decay affects spike frequency and curvature growth in normalized networks.

record.problems: Most training-loss trajectories are presented as figures without numeric spike counts or uncertainty estimates. The large-scale Transformer result uses one reported setup; the text does not report repeated-run variation.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were omitted.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, learning speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, divergence at larger rates, sustained sharpness hovering while loss falls, and divergence from an initially subthreshold rate.
BatchNorm's accuracy gains per training time and comparative learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparable speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern effects outside the listed versions. Their states are therefore cannot_determine relative to those versions; this does not dispute the reported weight-decay effects. The supplied text does not justify interpreting loss spikes as divergence or as evidence of recovery above an initial stability limit.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 label conditions, model size, and training duration.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width.
Depth comparisons, plain versus residual shortcuts, and training error.
Learning-rate sweeps above the initial stability limit, recovery, and sharpness behavior at the stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: LLaMA-style Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained for one epoch while sweeping weight decay over {0, 0.5, 1}.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory; paper reports more frequent spikes with larger weight decay.
rows.value: Larger weight decay leads to more frequent loss spikes.
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the figure caption and paper text; individual spike counts are not stated.
rows.check: Spike frequency under weight-decay sweeps does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 using SGD while varying weight decay.

conditions.value: varied; values not stated in text

rows.measure: Training loss trajectory; paper reports more frequent spikes with larger weight decay.
rows.value: Larger weight decay leads to more frequent loss spikes.
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the figure caption; individual spike counts are not stated.
rows.check: Loss spikes do not establish training classification error or V5 dynamics. Figure 1b supplies decay values 0, 0.001 and 0.01.

rows.subject: Fully connected neural network without normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with SGD and weight decay, without normalization.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and loss spikes.
rows.value: Weight decay at a fixed level does not reliably induce loss spikes when the learning rate is modest.
rows.note: This is the no-normalization comparison condition.
rows.check: Figure 2a shows decay settings 0, 0.001, 0.01 and 0.03, despite the appendix's fixed-level wording. Absence of spikes at one learning rate does not measure V6's speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with SGD while sweeping weight decay.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and loss spikes.
rows.value: Increasing weight decay induces pronounced loss spikes in models equipped with normalization layers.
rows.note: Weight decay was not applied to normalization layers.
rows.check: Weight-decay-induced spikes with BatchNorm do not measure accuracy gains or comparative learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Fully connected neural network with LayerNorm
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with SGD while sweeping weight decay.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and loss spikes.
rows.value: Increasing weight decay induces pronounced loss spikes in models equipped with normalization layers.
rows.note: Weight decay was not applied to normalization layers.
rows.check: LayerNorm spike behavior does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: Five-layer fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST under varying weight decay; plotted training trajectories and endpoint Hessian sharpness.
rows.measure: Largest Hessian eigenvalue at training endpoint.
rows.note: Values and conditions are given in the figure; the text says increasing weight decay leads to a larger maximum eigenvalue.
rows.check: Endpoint curvature under different decay settings cannot establish V5's temporal dynamics. The supplied figure text concatenates the final eigenvalue with adjacent plot text, so the reported value 386 needs visual verification.

rows.subject: Three-layer fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.size_stated: Three-layer FNN; hidden width not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained with full-batch gradient descent on the synthetic regression target while sweeping weight decay.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and loss spikes.
rows.value: Increasing weight decay can induce pronounced loss spikes during training.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes pronounced spikes.
rows.check: Full-batch squared-loss spikes under a decay sweep do not establish recovery above the initial stability limit, threshold hovering, or below-threshold initialization followed by divergence.

rows.subject: Three-layer fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.size_stated: Three-layer FNN; hidden width not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured largest Hessian eigenvalue at the training endpoint under different weight-decay settings.
rows.measure: Largest Hessian eigenvalue at training endpoint.
rows.note: Figure caption says λmax denotes the largest eigenvalue at the endpoint.
rows.check: Endpoint eigenvalues do not establish V5's trajectory relative to the stability threshold.

rows.subject: Three-layer fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.size_stated: Three-layer FNN; hidden width not stated
rows.operation_detail: Rescaled scale-invariant parameters while holding non-scale-invariant parameters fixed; measured the full Hessian's top eigenvalue.
rows.measure: Largest eigenvalue of the full Hessian as a function of scaling factor.
rows.value: λmax increases sharply as the scaling factor decreases.
rows.note: Paper states this result in its discussion of the controlled scaling experiment.
rows.check: Controlled parameter rescaling measures curvature scaling, not training recovery or threshold-hovering dynamics.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Rescaled convolutional weights immediately followed by BatchNorm while holding BatchNorm parameters and classifier fixed; measured the full Hessian's top eigenvalue.
rows.measure: Largest eigenvalue of the full Hessian as a function of scaling factor.
rows.value: λmax increases rapidly as the scaling factor decreases, consistent with the theoretical lower bound.
rows.note: The paper notes residual connections preclude strict layer-wise scale invariance.
rows.check: Controlled parameter rescaling measures curvature scaling, not any listed training effect.

rows.subject: Three-layer fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.size_stated: Three-layer FNN; hidden width not stated
rows.operation_detail: Tracked Hessian eigenvalues for scale-invariant, non-scale-invariant, and full parameter blocks during training.
rows.measure: Largest Hessian eigenvalue for parameter blocks and full parameter space.
rows.baseline: At initialization, the scale-invariant block eigenvalue is smaller than the non-scale-invariant block eigenvalue.
rows.value: The scale-invariant block eigenvalue increases, surpasses the non-scale-invariant block, and becomes the dominant contribution to global λmax.
rows.note: The text describes the temporal pattern qualitatively.
rows.check: Changing dominance of Hessian blocks does not establish threshold hovering while loss falls or the other V5 outcomes.

rows.subject: Fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.operation_detail: Compared first-layer weight norm with its predicted spike boundary during late training.
rows.measure: Temporal alignment between sustained boundary crossings and training-loss spikes.
rows.value: Pronounced loss spikes align with sustained excursions below the predicted boundary.
rows.note: The plot uses a filtering protocol: merge intervals separated by fewer than 30 iterations and discard intervals shorter than 200 iterations.
rows.check: This is the MNIST classification network, not the synthetic toy network. The plotted boundary is the gradient-direction spike boundary; its filtered alignment with spikes does not establish a listed version.

rows.subject: Fully connected neural network with BatchNorm
rows.operation_detail: Compared first-layer weight norm with its predicted spike boundary during training.
rows.measure: Temporal alignment between sustained boundary crossings and training-loss spikes.
rows.value: Pronounced loss spikes align with sustained excursions below the predicted boundary.
rows.note: The plot uses a filtering protocol: merge intervals separated by fewer than 30 iterations and discard intervals shorter than 200 iterations.
rows.check: The plotted boundary is the gradient-direction spike boundary. The explicit 30/200-iteration filtering rule is specified for Figure 7a, not independently for Figure 7b.

rows.subject: Four-layer, single-head Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdamW on synthetic next-token prediction while sweeping weight decay.
rows.value: Varying weight decay leads to markedly different optimization dynamics.
rows.note: The text does not specify which plotted settings spike or diverge.
rows.check: Different optimization dynamics under weight decay do not establish a listed effect; partial is not a verdict on any claim version.

rows.subject: LLaMA-style Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared standard weight decay on all parameters with weight decay disabled for MLP parameters.

conditions.value: 3 for all parameters versus excluded for MLP parameters

rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and loss-spike frequency.
rows.value: With weight decay disabled for MLP parameters, spike frequency is reduced and training loss attains lower values.
rows.note: This is an intervention on which parameters receive weight decay.
rows.check: Reduced spike frequency and lower loss after excluding MLP parameters from decay do not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: Three-layer fully connected neural network with normalization
rows.operation_detail: Applied weight decay exclusively to non-scale-invariant layers.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and loss spikes.
rows.baseline: standard setting with weight decay applied to all layers
rows.value: Stability improves significantly; loss spikes are effectively suppressed, including under relatively large learning rates and weight decay.
rows.note: The appendix describes the comparison as an ablation.
rows.check: Suppressing spikes by changing which parameters receive decay does not establish V5 recovery or V6 learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Three-layer fully connected neural network with normalization
rows.operation_detail: Measured endpoint maximum Hessian eigenvalue when weight decay was applied only to non-scale-invariant layers.
rows.measure: Largest Hessian eigenvalue at training endpoint.
rows.value: Does not exhibit a clear increasing trend as weight decay strength increases.
rows.note: The text explicitly reports no clear increasing trend.
rows.check: Absence of a decay-dependent endpoint sharpness trend is not absence of a listed effect; endpoint sharpness cannot establish V5's temporal behavior.
